text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia is striving for NATO membership because it is a natural step not because it is frightened of Russia, Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves told the NACC meeting in Brussels.

- A group of Russian experts on humanitarian and legal issues ended a visit to Estonia to look at the situation of Russian-speakers in the country without presenting any demands. They are expected to compile recommendations for the Estonian government.
- Chechen commander Salman Raduyev says in an interview that Dzokhar Dudayev is being treated for wounds in a hospital in Europe.
- The government does not intend to intervene in the labour disputes in the plants of Kreenholm and Silmet in northeastern Estonia.
- Central bank president Vahur Kraft said in a booklet on Estonia's monetary policy that inflation in 1997 will be around 13 percent to 15 percent.
- Parliament approved amendments to the law on government, cutting the number of separate departments but keeping the medicines and tourism department.
